Theme

Civic life: news, government & the law

court noun

of law

also court of law, law court, courtroom, courthouse, go to court, take to court, in court, the courts, justice system, bring to justice, hold court, sit as judge, take someone to court, bring to court

classical

Nep. Epam. 8.2: in jūdicium vēnit
Quint. 4.2.25 (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 194
Traupman 298

jūdicium, jūdiciī n.

noun, second declension

a court of justice; the trial held in it

Properly the trial, and by extension the court that holds it (Lewis & Short). To take someone to court, in jūdicium vocāre (Cic. Balb. 64, Lewis & Short) or addūcere (Traupman 194).

Other words

  • in jūs vocāre — summon to court; with īre or ambulāre, go to court

    phrase: jūs, jūris n. (the court) with in and the accusative · also used · classical · Ter. Ph. 936: in jūs ambulā; Hor. S. 1.9.77: rapit in jūs; Cic. Verr. 2.2.187 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 197: in jūs īre, to go on trial

    The summons before the praetor that began a lawsuit; jūs here is the place where justice is given (Lewis & Short).

  • tribūnal, tribūnālis n. — the judgment seat, the bench

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Verr. 2.2.94 (Lewis & Short); Liv. 26.22.3: ad tribūnal cōnsulis vēnit (Lewis & Short); M-O s.v. court

    The raised platform on which the magistrate sat to give judgment; Morgan–Owens gives it for a court.

  • basilica, basilicae f. — courthouse

    noun, first declension · also used · classical · Liv. 39.44.7 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 174, 190, 194; Traupman 298

    The colonnaded hall in the forum where courts sat and business was done, such as the basilica Jūlia (Lewis & Short); Traupman’s word for a courthouse.

  • jūs dīcere — to hold court, sit as judge, administer justice

    also used · classical · Cic. Fam. 13.14: ā Volcātiō, quī Rōmae jūs dīcit (Lewis & Short s.v. jūs); Traupman 190, 194, 195

Examples

  • In jūs ambulā.

    Come to court!Ter. Ph. 936

  • At ille in jūdicium vēnit, nihil eōrum negāvit, quae adversāriī crīminī dabant

    But he came into court, and denied none of the things his opponents charged him withNep. Epam. 8.2

  • rapit in jūs; clāmor utrimque, undique concursus

    he hauls him off to court; shouting on both sides, people running up from everywhereHor. S. 1.9.77–78

  • aliquem in jūdicium addūcere

    to take someone to courtTraupman 194, 197

  • Quis jūs dīcēbat?

    Who presided as judge?Traupman 190

  • jūs dīcere

    to hold courtTraupman 298

  • aliquem in jūdicium vocāre (addūcere)

    to take someone to courtTraupman 298

See also trial, lawyer, witness, case, law.
